title.zh: 卷六十一 志第三十: 刑法上
title.raw: 卷六十一 志第三十: 刑法上 Volume 61 Treatises 31: Punishment and Law 1

sentences.zh: 刑法志上

translations.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and Law, Part One

sentences.zh: 刑也者，始於兵而終於禮者也。

translations.literal: Punishment is that which begins with military force and ends with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment begins with arms and ends with ritual — that is its nature.

sentences.zh: 鴻荒之代，生民有兵，如蜂有螫，自衛而已。

translations.literal: In the age of primordial chaos, the living people had arms, like bees have stings — for self-defense alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest ages, people bore arms as bees bear stings — solely to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 蚩尤惟始作亂，斯民鴟義，奸宄並作，刑之用豈能已乎？

translations.literal: Only when Chiyou first raised rebellion did this people turn fierce and lawless; treachery and wickedness arose together — how could the use of punishment ever cease?
translations.idiomatic: When Chiyou first rose in revolt, the people turned violent and treacherous; with crime rampant, how could punishment be set aside?

sentences.zh: 帝堯清問下民，乃命三後恤功於民，伯夷降典，折民惟刑，故曰刑也者，始於兵而終於禮者也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yao inquired deeply among the people below, then ordered the Three Lords to show concern for the people's achievements, and Boyi brought down the statutes, adjudicating the people solely by punishment — hence it is said that punishment begins with military force and ends with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao sought the people's counsel and charged the Three Lords to care for their welfare; Boyi issued the penal code and judged the people by law alone — hence the saying that punishment begins with arms and ends with ritual.

sentences.zh: 先王順天地四時以建六卿。

translations.literal: The former kings followed Heaven and Earth and the four seasons in establishing the Six Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings aligned the Six Ministries with Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 秋，刑官也，象時之成物焉。

translations.literal: Autumn is the minister of punishment, symbolizing the season's completion of things.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn is the season of punishment, when the harvest is gathered in.

sentences.zh: 秋傳氣於夏，變色於春，推可知也。

translations.literal: Autumn transmits its qi from summer and changes color from spring — by extension this may be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn draws its force from summer and takes its hue from spring — from this one may infer the rest.

sentences.zh: 遼以用武立國，禁暴戢奸，莫先於刑。

translations.literal: Liao established its state by the use of arms; to restrain violence and suppress wickedness, nothing comes before punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao founded their state by force of arms; to curb violence and suppress crime, punishment came first.

sentences.zh: 國初制法，有出於五服、三就之外者，兵之勢方張，禮之用未遑也。

translations.literal: When the state was first founded and laws were made, some provisions went beyond the five degrees of mourning kinship and the three places of exile — the momentum of arms was still expanding, and the application of ritual had not yet been attended to.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the realm, some laws went beyond the traditional five degrees of kinship and three places of exile — military power was still ascendant, and ritual governance had yet to take hold.

sentences.zh: 及阻午可汗知宗室雅裏之賢，命為夷離堇以掌刑辟，豈非士師之官，非賢者不可為乎？

translations.literal: When Khan Zuwu recognized the worth of Yali of the imperial clan, he appointed him yilijin to oversee criminal matters — was this not the office of the Minister of Punishment, which none but the worthy could hold?
translations.idiomatic: When Khan Zuwu saw the talent of Yali in the imperial house, he made him yilijin to oversee justice — was this not the post of chief judge, fit only for a man of merit?

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗經理疆土，擐甲之士歲無寧居，威克厥愛，理勢然也。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong administered the realm's territory; men in armor had no peaceful year — severity overcame kindness, as reason and circumstance demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu and Taizong, who consolidated the realm, armored men knew no year of rest — severity prevailed over mercy, as the times required.

sentences.zh: 子孫相繼，其法互有輕重；

translations.literal: Their descendants succeeded one another, and their laws varied in severity and leniency;
translations.idiomatic: Successive rulers inherited the throne, and the laws varied in severity;

sentences.zh: 中間能審權宜，終之以禮者，惟景、聖二宗為優耳。

translations.literal: Among them, only the Jing and Sheng emperors, who could weigh expedients and conclude with ritual propriety, were truly superior.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who could weigh circumstances wisely and bring punishment to rest in ritual, only the Jing and Sheng emperors stand out.

sentences.zh: 然其制刑之凡有四：曰死，曰流，曰徒，曰杖。

translations.literal: Yet in general their punishments were of four kinds: death, exile, penal servitude, and beating.
translations.idiomatic: Their penal system, however, had four main categories: death, exile, penal servitude, and corporal beating.

sentences.zh: 死刑有絞、斬、淩遲之屬，又有籍沒之法。

translations.literal: Capital punishment included strangulation, decapitation, and dismemberment by slow slicing, and there was also the law of confiscation and enslavement.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes were punished by strangulation, beheading, or lingchi, and there was also confiscation of property and kin.

sentences.zh: 流刑量罪輕重，置之邊城部族之地，遠則投諸境外，又遠則罰使絕域。

translations.literal: Exile was meted according to the severity of the crime, placing offenders in border towns and tribal lands; farther still, they were cast beyond the frontier; farther yet, they were punished by dispatch to the remotest regions.
translations.idiomatic: Exile was graded by offense: lesser crimes sent one to border garrisons and tribal lands; graver ones beyond the frontier; the gravest to the farthest reaches of the empire.

sentences.zh: 徒刑一曰終身，二曰五年，三曰一年半；

translations.literal: Penal servitude was of three terms: one called lifetime, one five years, and one a year and a half;
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude had three terms: lifetime, five years, and eighteen months;

sentences.zh: 終身者決五百，其次遞減百；

translations.literal: for lifetime, five hundred strokes were decreed; for the next term, one hundred fewer in succession;
translations.idiomatic: the lifetime term carried five hundred strokes, with each lesser term reduced by one hundred;

sentences.zh: 又有黥刺之法。

translations.literal: there was also the method of tattooing and branding.
translations.idiomatic: and branding and tattooing were also prescribed.

sentences.zh: 仗刑自五十至三百，凡杖五十以上者，以沙袋決之；

translations.literal: Beating ranged from fifty to three hundred strokes; for all beatings of fifty strokes or more, the sandbag was used to administer them;
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment ran from fifty to three hundred strokes; for fifty strokes or more, the sandbag cudgel was used;

sentences.zh: 又有木劍、大棒、鐵骨朵之法。

translations.literal: there were also the methods of the wooden sword, the great club, and the iron mace.
translations.idiomatic: along with the wooden sword, great club, and iron mace.

sentences.zh: 木劍、大棒之數三，自十五至三十，鐵骨朵之數，或五、或七。

translations.literal: The wooden sword and great club had three gradations, from fifteen to thirty strokes; the iron mace was applied in numbers of either five or seven.
translations.idiomatic: The wooden sword and great club had three grades, from fifteen to thirty blows; the iron mace was used in sets of five or seven.

sentences.zh: 有重罪者，將決以沙袋，先於脽骨之上及四周擊之。

translations.literal: For those with grave offenses about to be sentenced with the sandbag, blows were first struck upon the buttocks and all around them.
translations.idiomatic: Before a heavy sandbag sentence was carried out, blows were first delivered to the buttocks and surrounding area.

sentences.zh: 拷訊之具，有粗、細杖及鞭、烙法。

translations.literal: Instruments for interrogation included thick and thin rods, as well as the methods of whipping and branding.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation employed thick and thin rods, whipping, and branding.

sentences.zh: 粗杖之數二十；

translations.literal: the thick rod was applied in a count of twenty;
translations.idiomatic: The thick rod: twenty strokes;

sentences.zh: 細杖之數三，自三十至於六十。

translations.literal: the thin rod had three gradations, from thirty to sixty.
translations.idiomatic: the thin rod: three grades, from thirty to sixty strokes.

sentences.zh: 鞭、烙之數，凡烙三十者鞭三百，烙五十者鞭五百。

translations.literal: For whipping and branding, whoever received thirty brands was whipped three hundred times; whoever received fifty brands was whipped five hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: Branding and whipping were paired: thirty brands meant three hundred lashes; fifty brands meant five hundred.

sentences.zh: 被告諸事應伏而不服者，以此訊之。

translations.literal: When the accused in any matter ought to confess but would not submit, they were examined by these means.
translations.idiomatic: Defendants who should have confessed but refused were interrogated by these methods.

sentences.zh: 品官公事誤犯，民年七十以上、十五以下犯罪者，聽以贖論。

translations.literal: Ranked officials who erred in public duties, and commoners seventy years of age or above or fifteen and below who committed offenses, were permitted to redeem punishment by payment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who erred in office, and commoners over seventy or under fifteen who committed crimes, were allowed to commute their sentences by fine.

sentences.zh: 贖銅之數，杖一百者，輸錢千。

translations.literal: The scale for redeeming with copper: for one hundred strokes of the rod, one thousand coins were paid.
translations.idiomatic: The redemption tariff was set at one thousand cash for every hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 亦有八議、八縱之法。

translations.literal: There were also the Eight Privileges and the Eight Pardons.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Privileges and Eight Pardons were also in force.

sentences.zh: 籍沒之法，始自太祖為撻馬狘沙裏時，奉痕德堇可汗命，按於越釋魯遇害事，以其首惡家屬沒入瓦裏。

translations.literal: The law of confiscation began when Taizu, as tamag yaglashi, received orders from Khan Hendejin to investigate the murder of Yuyue Shilu, and the chief culprit's household was confiscated into the wali.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscation began when Taizu, still tamag yaglashi, was ordered by Khan Hendejin to investigate the murder of Yuyue Shilu; the ringleader's family was seized and enrolled in the wali.

sentences.zh: 及淳欽皇后時析出，以為著帳郎君，至世宗詔免之。

translations.literal: Under Empress Chunqin they were separated out and made registered-account gentlemen; by Shizong's edict they were finally exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Chunqin they were set apart as registered-account gentlemen; Shizong later issued an edict releasing them.

sentences.zh: 其後內外戚屬及世官之家，犯反逆等罪，復沒入焉；

translations.literal: Afterward, when collateral kin inside and outside the clan and hereditary official households committed crimes such as treason, they were again confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: Later, collateral kin and hereditary official families convicted of treason and like crimes were again subject to confiscation;

sentences.zh: 餘人則沒為著帳戶；

translations.literal: the rest were confiscated as registered-account households;
translations.idiomatic: others were reduced to registered-account households;

sentences.zh: 其沒入宮分、分賜臣下者亦有之。

translations.literal: some were confiscated into the palace estates, and some were distributed as gifts to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: some property went to the palace treasury, some was distributed among officials.

sentences.zh: 木劍、大棒者，太宗時制。

translations.literal: The wooden sword and great club were instituted in Taizong's time.
translations.idiomatic: The wooden sword and great club were introduced under Taizong.

sentences.zh: 木劍面平背隆，大臣犯重罪，欲寬宥則擊之。

translations.literal: The wooden sword had a flat face and a raised back; when great ministers committed grave offenses and the emperor wished to show leniency, they were struck with it.
translations.idiomatic: The wooden sword was flat on one side and ridged on the other; when a senior minister merited death but the emperor wished mercy, he was struck with this instead.

sentences.zh: 沙袋者，穆宗時制，其制用熟皮合縫之，長六寸，廣二寸，柄一尺許。

translations.literal: The sandbag was instituted in Muzong's time; it was made of cured leather sewn together, six inches long, two inches wide, with a handle about one foot.
translations.idiomatic: The sandbag cudgel was introduced under Muzong: cured leather sewn into a bag six inches long and two inches wide, on a handle about a foot long.

sentences.zh: 徒刑之數詳於重熙制，杖刑以下之數詳於咸雍制；

translations.literal: The numbers for penal servitude are detailed in the Chongxi regulations; the numbers for beating and below are detailed in the Xianyong regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude was codified in detail under the Chongxi code; corporal punishments and lesser penalties under the Xianyong code;

sentences.zh: 其餘非常用而無定式者，不可殫紀。

translations.literal: as for the rest that were not in regular use and had no fixed form, they cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: the rest — irregular punishments without fixed rules — are too numerous to list in full.

sentences.zh: 太祖初年，庶事草創，犯罪者量輕重決之。

translations.literal: In Taizu's early years, when all affairs were still being established, offenders were judged according to the severity of their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's early reign, with institutions still taking shape, offenders were sentenced according to the gravity of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 其後治諸弟逆黨，權宜立法。

translations.literal: Later, in punishing the rebellious faction of his younger brothers, he made laws as expedients required.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in suppressing his brothers' rebellion, he enacted ad hoc laws suited to the emergency.

sentences.zh: 親王從逆，不磬諸甸人，或投高崖殺之；

translations.literal: Imperial princes who followed the rebellion were not executed by the qing method before the assembled people of the domains, but were sometimes cast from high cliffs to their death;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes who joined the revolt were not publicly executed before the assembled domains, but were sometimes hurled from high cliffs;

sentences.zh: 淫亂不軌者，五車轘殺之；

translations.literal: those guilty of licentiousness and misconduct were killed by drawing and quartering with five carts;
translations.idiomatic: those guilty of sexual misconduct were torn apart by five teams of horses;

sentences.zh: 逆父母者視此；

translations.literal: those who defied their parents were treated likewise;
translations.idiomatic: those who defied their parents received the same punishment;

sentences.zh: 訕詈犯上者，以熟鐵錐摏其口殺之。

translations.literal: those who slandered and reviled their superiors were killed by driving a heated iron awl through the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: those who slandered their superiors were killed by driving a red-hot iron spike through the mouth.

sentences.zh: 從坐者，量罪輕重杖決。

translations.literal: Accomplices were beaten according to the severity of their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplices were beaten in proportion to their guilt.

sentences.zh: 杖有二：大者重錢五百，小者三百。

translations.literal: There were two kinds of beating: the great rod weighed five hundred cash, the small three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Two grades of rod were used: the heavy rod weighed five hundred cash, the light three hundred.

sentences.zh: 又為梟磔、生瘞、射鬼箭、炮擲、支解之刑。

translations.literal: He also established the punishments of exposure of the head, dismemberment, live burial, shooting with ghost arrows, cannon-throwing, and hacking apart.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted exposure of the head, dismemberment, live burial, ghost-arrow execution, catapulting, and hacking to pieces.

sentences.zh: 歸於重法，閑民使不為變耳。

translations.literal: All this came under severe law, to keep the common people from making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: These harsh measures were meant to keep the common people from stirring trouble.

sentences.zh: 歲癸酉，下詔曰：「朕自北征以來，四方獄訟，積滯頗多。

translations.literal: In the year guiyou, an edict was issued: "Since Our northern campaigns began, lawsuits from the four quarters have piled up in considerable backlog.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year, an edict declared: "Since our northern campaigns began, lawsuits from across the realm have piled up in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 今休戰息民，群臣其副朕意，詳決之，無或冤枉。

translations.literal: Now that warfare has ceased and the people rest, let the ministers assist Our intent, adjudicate carefully, and allow no wrongful conviction."
translations.idiomatic: Now that war has ceased and the people may rest, let my ministers assist my intent, judge cases carefully, and permit no wrongful conviction."

sentences.zh: 」乃命北府宰相蕭敵魯等分道疏決。

translations.literal: He then ordered Northern Chancellery Chief Minister Xiao Dilu and others to clear the backlog by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Northern Chancellery Chief Minister Xiao Dilu and others to clear the backlog in separate jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 有遼欽恤之意，昉見於此。

translations.literal: The Liao's intent of compassionate review first appeared in this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao concern for compassionate review of cases first appears here.

sentences.zh: 神冊六年，克定諸夷，上謂侍臣曰：「凡國家庶務，巨細各殊，若憲度不明，則何以為治，群下亦何由知禁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shence, after subduing the various tribes, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "In all the state's common affairs, great and small each differ — if statutes and measures are not clear, how can there be governance, and how can subordinates know what is forbidden?"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shence, after pacifying the tribes, the emperor told his attendants: "State affairs great and small all differ — if the laws are unclear, how can the realm be governed, and how can subjects know what is forbidden?"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔大臣定治契丹及諸夷之法，漢人則斷以《律令》，仍置鐘院以達民冤。

translations.literal: He then ordered the great ministers to fix laws for governing the Khitan and the various tribes; Han Chinese were to be judged by the Statutes and Ordinances, and the Bell Court was still established so the people's grievances could reach him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his ministers to codify laws for the Khitan and other tribes; Han subjects were to be judged under the Tang code, and the Bell Court was established so the people's grievances could reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 至太宗時，治渤海人一依漢法，余無改焉。

translations.literal: By Taizong's time, the Bohai people were governed entirely by Han law; the rest remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, the Bohai were governed entirely by Han law; otherwise the system was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 會同四年，皇族舍利郎君謀毒通事解裏等，已中者二人，命重杖之，及其妻流於厥拔離弭河，族造藥者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huitong, Imperial Clan Sheli Langjun plotted to poison the Interpreter Jieli and others; two had already been poisoned. He was ordered severely beaten, and his wife was exiled to the Juebalimi River; the clan of those who made the drug was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huitong, Imperial Clan Sheli Langjun plotted to poison Interpreter Jieli and others; two victims had already succumbed. He was heavily beaten, his wife exiled to the Juebalimi River, and the poison-makers' clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 世宗天祿二年，天德、蕭翰、劉哥及其弟盆都等謀反，天德伏誅，杖翰，流劉哥，遣盆都使轄戛斯國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianlu under Shizong, Tiande, Xiao Han, Liuge, and Liuge's younger brother Pendu and others plotted rebellion. Tiande was executed, Han was beaten, Liuge was exiled, and Pendu was sent as envoy to the Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizong's second year of Tianlu, Tiande, Xiao Han, Liuge, and Liuge's brother Pendu plotted rebellion. Tiande was executed, Han beaten, Liuge exiled, and Pendu dispatched as envoy to the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 夫四人之罪均而刑異，遼之世，同罪異論者蓋多。

translations.literal: These four men's crimes were equal yet their punishments differed — in the Liao age, cases of equal guilt but differing sentences were indeed numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Though the four men's crimes were equal, their punishments differed — under the Liao, equal guilt often received unequal sentences.

sentences.zh: 穆宗應歷十二年，國舅帳郎君蕭延之奴海裏強陵拽剌禿裏年未及之女，以法無文，加之宮刑，仍付禿裏以為奴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yingli under Muzong, the slave Haili of Imperial Uncle-in-Law Tent Langjun Xiao Yan forcibly violated the daughter of Zhuala Tulii, who had not yet reached the age of maturity. Because the law had no provision, he was subjected to castration and handed over to Tulii as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: In Muzong's twelfth year of Yingli, slave Haili of Imperial Uncle-in-Law Tent Langjun Xiao Yan raped Zhuala Tulii's underage daughter. With no statute covering the offense, he was castrated and given to Tulii as a slave.

sentences.zh: 因著為令。

translations.literal: This was then written into law.
translations.idiomatic: The case was then codified as precedent.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭有司：「自先朝行幸頓次，必高立標識以禁行者。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he instructed the officials: "Since former dynasties made imperial progresses and encampments, markers were always erected high to forbid passage.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixteenth year, he instructed officials: "On imperial progresses since former times, tall markers were erected to bar unauthorized passage.

sentences.zh: 比聞楚古輩，故低置其標深草中，利人誤入，因之取財。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that Chugu and his ilk deliberately set their markers low in deep grass, profiting when people strayed in by mistake and then extorting them.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that Chugu and his ilk deliberately set markers low in deep grass, profiting when travelers strayed in by mistake and then extorting them.

sentences.zh: 自今有復然者，以死論。

translations.literal: From now on, whoever does so again shall be sentenced to death."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who does so again shall be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」然帝嗜酒及獵，不恤政事，五坊、掌獸、近侍、奉膳、掌酒人等以獐鹿、野豕、鶻雉之屬亡失傷斃，及私歸逃亡，在告逾期，召不時至，或以奏對少不如意，或以飲食細故，或因犯者遷怒無辜，輒加炮烙鐵梳之刑。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was addicted to wine and hunting and paid no heed to government. Men of the Five Wards, keepers of beasts, close attendants, food servers, wine stewards, and the like — for lost, injured, or dead roe deer, wild boar, falcon-hunted pheasants, and such; for unauthorized departure or flight; for overstaying leave; for failing to appear when summoned — or because answers at audience displeased him slightly, or because of trifles in food and drink, or because he vented anger on the innocent because of an offender — he would at once apply branding-iron torture and iron-comb punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor cared only for wine and the hunt, neglecting government. Keepers of the Five Wards, animal handlers, attendants, food servers, and wine stewards — for lost or injured game, unauthorized absence, overstayed leave, or tardiness when summoned; for answers at audience that displeased him, trifles at table, or rage vented on the innocent because of another's fault — he would at once apply branding and iron-comb torture.

sentences.zh: 甚者至於無算。

translations.literal: In extreme cases the count was beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the worst cases the toll was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 或以手刃刺之，斬擊射燎，斷手足，爛肩股，折腰脛，劃口碎齒，棄屍於野。

translations.literal: Sometimes he stabbed them with his own hand, hacked and shot and burned them, severed hands and feet, mangled shoulders and thighs, broke waists and shins, slashed mouths and shattered teeth, and cast the corpses into the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he stabbed them himself, hacked, shot, and burned them, severed limbs, mangled shoulders and thighs, broke backs and shins, slashed mouths and shattered teeth, and left the corpses in the open country.

sentences.zh: 且命築封於其地，死者至百有餘人。

translations.literal: He even ordered mounds built and sealed on the spot; the dead reached more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He even ordered burial mounds raised on the spot; the dead numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 京師置百尺牢以處系囚。

translations.literal: In the capital a hundred-foot prison was set up to hold bound prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital a hundred-foot prison was built to hold detainees.

sentences.zh: 蓋其即位未久，惑女巫肖古之言，取人膽合延年藥，故殺人頗眾。

translations.literal: This was because not long after he took the throne he was deluded by the words of the shamaness Xiaogu, who said human gallbladders were needed to compound an elixir of longevity — hence he killed many people.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after his accession he was swayed by the shamaness Xiaogu, who claimed human gall was needed for an elixir of longevity — hence the many killings.

sentences.zh: 後悟其詐，以鳴鏑叢射、騎踐殺之。

translations.literal: Later, realizing her deceit, he had her shot in volleys with whistling arrows and trampled to death under horses.
translations.idiomatic: When he realized her fraud, he had her shot with whistling arrows and trampled under horses.

sentences.zh: 及海裏之死，為長夜之飲，五坊、掌獸人等及左右給事誅戮者，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: After Haili's death he held all-night drinking; men of the Five Wards, beast keepers, and attendants on left and right who were executed followed one upon another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Haili's execution he held all-night revels, and executions among the Five Wards, beast keepers, and personal attendants continued without pause.

sentences.zh: 雖嘗悔其因怒濫刑，諭大臣切諫，在廷畏懦，鮮能匡救，雖諫又不能聽。

translations.literal: Although he once regretted his angry excess in punishment and instructed the great ministers to remonstrate earnestly, those at court were timid and few could rescue victims; even when they remonstrated, he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Though he once regretted his angry excesses and urged his ministers to remonstrate, the court was timid and few could save victims; even when they spoke up, he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 當其將殺壽哥、念古，殿前都點檢耶律夷臘葛諫曰：「壽哥等斃所掌雉，畏罪而亡，法不應死。

translations.literal: When he was about to execute Shouge and Nian'gu, Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige remonstrated: "Shouge and the others let the pheasants in their charge die; fearing punishment they fled — by law they should not die."
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to execute Shouge and Nian'gu, Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige remonstrated: "Shouge and the others let their pheasants die and fled in fear of punishment — by law they do not deserve death."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，斬壽哥等支解之。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and beheaded Shouge and the others, hacking them apart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, beheaded Shouge and the others, and had them hacked apart.

sentences.zh: 命有司盡取鹿人之在系者凡六十五人，斬所犯重者四十四人，余悉痛杖之。

translations.literal: He ordered the officials to take all deer keepers in custody, sixty-five in all; forty-four of the gravest offenders were beheaded, and the rest were all severely beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all sixty-five deer keepers in custody seized; forty-four of the worst offenders were beheaded, the rest severely beaten.

sentences.zh: 中有欲置死者，賴王子必攝等諫得免。

translations.literal: Among them some were about to be put to death, but were spared thanks to remonstrance by Princes Bishe and others.
translations.idiomatic: Some who would have been executed were spared through remonstrance by Princes Bishe and others.

sentences.zh: 已而怒頗德飼鹿不時，致傷而斃，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Soon after, angered that Pode fed the deer irregularly so that one was injured and died, he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, enraged that Pode had fed the deer irregularly, causing one to be injured and die, he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 季年，暴虐益甚，嘗謂太尉化葛曰：「朕醉中有處決不當者，醒當覆奏。

translations.literal: In his later years his cruelty grew worse. He once told Grand Marshal Huage: "When I am drunk and pass judgments improperly, report them again when I am sober."
translations.idiomatic: In his final years his cruelty worsened. He once told Grand Marshal Huage: "When I pass improper judgments while drunk, report them again when I am sober."

sentences.zh: 」徒能言之，竟無悛意，故及於難。

translations.literal: He could speak the words but had no intent to reform — hence he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He could say the words but never meant to reform — and so met his end.

sentences.zh: 雖云虐止褻禦，上不及大臣，下不及百姓，然刑法之制，豈人主快情縱意之具邪！

translations.literal: Although it is said his cruelty was confined to those close at hand in the inner quarters, not reaching up to great ministers nor down to the common people, yet is the system of penal law an instrument for the ruler to indulge his feelings and give free rein to his will?
translations.idiomatic: Though his cruelty is said to have touched only those close at hand, not reaching ministers above or commoners below, is the penal code an instrument for a ruler to indulge his whims?

sentences.zh: 景宗在潛，已鑒其失。

translations.literal: Jingzong, while still heir apparent, had already taken these failures as a lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong, while still heir apparent, had already taken note of these excesses.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以宿衛失職，斬殿前都點檢耶律夷臘葛。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, because the palace guard had failed in duty, he beheaded Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession, citing dereliction of the palace guard, he beheaded Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige.

sentences.zh: 趙王喜隱自囚所擅去械鎖，求見自辯，語之曰：「枉直未分，焉有出獄自辯之理？

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Xiyin, on his own authority, removed his fetters and locks from the prison and sought an audience to plead his case. The emperor told him: "Right and wrong are not yet distinguished — how can there be grounds for leaving prison to plead one's case?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Xiyin removed his own shackles and sought an audience to plead his case. The emperor told him: "Guilt and innocence are not yet settled — what grounds have you to leave prison and plead?"

sentences.zh: 」命復縶之。

translations.literal: He ordered him bound again.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him bound again.

sentences.zh: 既而躬錄囚徒，盡召而釋之。

translations.literal: Soon after he personally reviewed the prisoners and summoned them all to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he personally reviewed the prisoners and released them all.

sentences.zh: 保寧三年，以穆宗廢鐘院，窮民有冤者無所訴，故詔復之，仍命鑄鐘，紀詔其上，道所以廢置之意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoning, because Muzong had abolished the Bell Court and the poor with grievances had nowhere to appeal, an edict restored it; he also ordered a bell cast and the edict inscribed upon it, stating the reasons for abolition and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoning, because Muzong had abolished the Bell Court and the poor had nowhere to appeal their grievances, Jingzong restored it, ordered a new bell cast, and had the edict inscribed upon it explaining why it had been abolished and restored.

sentences.zh: 吳王稍為奴所告，有司請鞫，帝曰：「朕知其誣，若按問，恐餘人效之。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Shao was denounced by a slave; the officials requested an investigation. The emperor said: "I know this is a false accusation — if we conduct an inquiry, I fear others will imitate it."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Shao was denounced by a slave; officials requested an investigation. The emperor said: "I know this is false — if we investigate, others may follow suit."

sentences.zh: 」命斬以徇。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the slave beheaded as a warning.

sentences.zh: 五年，近侍實魯裏誤觸神纛，法應死，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the close attendant Shiruli accidentally touched the sacred banner — by law he should have died, but he was beaten and released.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, attendant Shiruli accidentally touched the sacred banner — a capital offense by law, but he was beaten and released.

sentences.zh: 庶幾寬猛相濟。

translations.literal: Thus leniency and severity were in some measure balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Thus leniency and severity were balanced.

sentences.zh: 然緩於討賊，應歷逆黨至是始獲而誅焉，議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was slow in pursuing rebels; the Yingli faction of traitors were only now captured and executed — critics for this reason thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was slow to pursue rebels; the Yingli traitors were only now captured and executed — critics held this against him.

sentences.zh: 聖宗沖年嗣位，睿智皇后稱制，留心聽斷，嘗勸帝宜寬法律。

translations.literal: Shengzong succeeded the throne in his youth; the Wise Empress Dowager held regency, attended carefully to hearings and judgments, and once urged the emperor to lighten the laws.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong succeeded as a child; the Wise Empress Dowager held regency, attended carefully to judgments, and urged him to lighten the laws.

sentences.zh: 帝壯，益習國事，銳意於治。

translations.literal: When the emperor came of age, he grew ever more practiced in state affairs and was keen on good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he grew adept at statecraft and devoted himself to governance.

sentences.zh: 當時更定法令凡十數事，多合人心，其用刑又能詳慎。

translations.literal: At that time he revised statutes and ordinances in more than a dozen matters, most of which accorded with people's hearts; in applying punishment he was also careful and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He revised more than a dozen statutes, most of which won popular approval, and applied punishment with care and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹及漢人相毆致死，其法輕重不均，至是一等科之。

translations.literal: Previously, when Khitan and Han Chinese beat each other to death, the law's severity and leniency were unequal; now they were punished under a single standard.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Khitan and Han beat each other to death, the penalties differed; now both were punished alike.

sentences.zh: 統和十二年，詔契丹人犯十惡，亦斷以《律》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tonghe, an edict declared that when Khitan committed the Ten Abominations, they too were to be judged by the Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tonghe, an edict declared that Khitan who committed the Ten Abominations were also to be judged under the Tang code.

sentences.zh: 舊法，死囚屍市三日，至是一宿即聽收瘞。

translations.literal: By the old law, the corpses of condemned prisoners were exposed in the market for three days; now after one night burial was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, executed prisoners' corpses were displayed in the market for three days; now burial was permitted after a single night.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，詔主非犯謀反大逆及流死罪者，其奴婢無得告首；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict declared that for masters who had not committed treason, great sedition, or crimes of exile or death, their male and female slaves were not permitted to denounce them;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict declared that slaves might not denounce masters who had not committed treason, great sedition, or capital or exilable offenses;

sentences.zh: 若奴婢犯罪至死，聽送有司，其主無得擅殺。

translations.literal: if male or female slaves committed offenses warranting death, they were to be sent to the authorities; their masters were not permitted to kill them on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: if a slave merited death, the case was to be sent to the authorities; masters were forbidden to execute them privately.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以舊法，宰相、節度使世選之家子孫犯罪，徒杖如齊民，惟免黥面，詔自今但犯罪當黥，即準法同科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, under the old law, when descendants of hereditary-selection households of chancellors and military governors committed offenses, penal servitude and beating were like those for common people, only tattooing the face was exempted; an edict declared that from now on, whenever an offense warranted tattooing, they were to be punished by the same standard as the law.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, under the old law, descendants of hereditary chancellor and military governor families who committed crimes received the same penal servitude and beating as commoners, though facial tattooing was waived; an edict now required that whenever tattooing was warranted, they be punished like everyone else.

sentences.zh: 開泰八年，以竊盜贓滿十貫，為首者處死，其法太重，故增至二十五貫，其首處死，從者決流。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaitai, because stolen goods in theft reached ten strings of cash, the ringleader was put to death — the law was too severe, so it was increased to twenty-five strings; the ringleader was put to death, accomplices were sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaitai, theft of ten strings of cash had meant death for the ringleader — the penalty was judged too harsh, so the threshold was raised to twenty-five strings; the ringleader still faced death, accomplices exile.

sentences.zh: 嘗敕諸處刑獄有冤，不能申雪者，聽詣御史臺陳訴，委官覆問。

translations.literal: He once ordered that wherever prisons held the wrongfully convicted who could not clear themselves, they were permitted to appeal to the Censorate, and officials were commissioned to re-examine the cases.
translations.idiomatic: He once ordered that prisoners who could not clear wrongful convictions might appeal to the Censorate, with officials commissioned to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 往時大理寺獄訟，凡關覆奏者，以翰林學士、給事中、政事舍人詳決，至是始置少卿及正主之。

translations.literal: Formerly in lawsuits at the Court of Judicial Review, all matters requiring review and memorial to the throne were decided in detail by Hanlin Academicians, Supervising Secretaries, and Administrative Assistants; only now were a Vice Director and a chief presiding officer first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, Court of Judicial Review cases requiring imperial review were decided by Hanlin academicians, supervising secretaries, and administrative assistants; only now were a vice director and presiding officer appointed.

sentences.zh: 猶慮其未盡，而親為錄囚。

translations.literal: Still fearing this was not enough, he personally reviewed the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Still unsatisfied, he personally reviewed the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 數遣使詣諸道審決冤滯，如邢抱樸之屬，所至，人自以為無冤。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys to the various circuits to examine and decide stale wrongful cases; men like Xing Baopu, wherever they went, made people feel they had no grievance left unredressed.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly dispatched envoys to the circuits to clear stale wrongful cases; men like Xing Baopu left people feeling that nowhere did injustice remain.

sentences.zh: 五院部民有自壞鎧甲者，其長佛奴杖殺之，上怒其用法太峻，詔奪官。

translations.literal: Among the people of the Five Wards, one who had damaged his own armor on his own initiative was beaten to death by his chief Fonu; the emperor, angered that the law had been applied too harshly, ordered Fonu's dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: When a man of the Five Wards damaged his own armor, his chief Fonu beat him to death; the emperor, angered at such harsh application of the law, stripped Fonu of his post.

sentences.zh: 吏以故不敢酷。

translations.literal: Officials for this reason did not dare to be cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Officials thereafter dared not be cruel.

sentences.zh: 撻剌幹乃方十因醉言宮掖事，法當死，特貰其罪。

translations.literal: Tatala Gannai Fangshi, because while drunk he spoke of inner-palace affairs, should by law have died, but was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tatala Gannai Fangshi spoke of inner-palace matters while drunk — a capital offense by law, but he was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 五院部民偶遺火。

translations.literal: A man of the Five Wards accidentally started a fire.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the Five Wards accidentally started a fire.

sentences.zh: 延及木葉山兆域，亦當死，杖而釋之，因著為法。

translations.literal: It spread to the sacred precinct of Mount Muye; this too should have meant death, but he was beaten and released, and this was then written into law.
translations.idiomatic: The fire spread to the sacred precinct of Mount Muye — also a capital offense, but he was beaten and released, and the case was codified as precedent.

sentences.zh: 至於敵八哥始竊薊州王令謙家財，及覺，以刃刺令謙，幸不死。

translations.literal: As for Dibage, he first stole the property of Wang Lingqian of Jizhou; when discovered, he stabbed Lingqian with a blade — fortunately he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Dibage first stole the property of Wang Lingqian of Jizhou; when discovered, he stabbed Lingqian with a blade, but fortunately Lingqian survived.

sentences.zh: 有司擬以盜論，止加杖罪。

translations.literal: The officials proposed judging it as theft, but the emperor only added a beating offense.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed treating it as theft, but the emperor imposed only a beating.

sentences.zh: 又那母古犯竊盜者十有三次，皆以情不可恕，論棄市。

translations.literal: Also Namugu had committed theft thirteen times; in every case the circumstances were unforgivable, and he was sentenced to execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Namugu had committed theft thirteen times; each case was deemed unforgivable, and he was sentenced to public execution.

sentences.zh: 因詔自今三犯竊盜者，黥額、徒三年；

translations.literal: Hence an edict declared that from now on, for a third theft offense, the forehead was tattooed and penal servitude of three years imposed;
translations.idiomatic: An edict therefore declared that a third theft offense would bring forehead tattooing and three years' penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 四則黥面、徒五年；

translations.literal: a fourth offense brought tattooing the face and five years' penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: a fourth offense, facial tattooing and five years' penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 至於五則處死。

translations.literal: upon a fifth, execution.
translations.idiomatic: a fifth, death.

sentences.zh: 若是者，重輕適宜，足以示訓。

translations.literal: Such gradations of severity and leniency were fitting and sufficient to serve as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Such gradations were proportionate and sufficient to serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 近侍劉哥、烏古斯嘗從齊王妻而逃，以赦，後會千齡節出首，乃詔諸近侍、護衛集視而腰斬之。

translations.literal: Close attendants Liuge and Wugusi had once fled with the wife of the Prince of Qi; they were pardoned, but later at the Thousand-Age Festival they came forward to confess; he then ordered all close attendants and guards assembled to witness their execution by cutting at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Liuge and Wugusi had once fled with the Prince of Qi's wife; though pardoned, they confessed at the Thousand-Age Festival; the emperor then had all attendants and guards assembled to witness their execution by cutting in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 於是國無幸民，綱紀修舉，吏多奉職，人重犯法。

translations.literal: Thus the state had no men who counted on luck; discipline was restored, officials mostly performed their duties, and people feared breaking the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thus no one counted on luck to escape justice; discipline was restored, officials performed their duties, and the people feared breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 故統和中，南京及易、平二州以獄空聞。

translations.literal: Therefore during Tonghe, the Southern Capital and the two prefectures of Yi and Ping were famed for empty prisons.
translations.idiomatic: During Tonghe, the Southern Capital and the prefectures of Yi and Ping were famed for empty prisons.

sentences.zh: 至開泰五年，諸道皆獄空，有刑措之風焉。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Kaitai, every circuit had empty prisons — there was a wind of punishments set aside.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth year of Kaitai, every circuit reported empty prisons — a sign that punishments had fallen largely into disuse.

sentences.zh: 故事，樞密使非國家重務，未嘗親決，凡獄訟惟夷離畢主之。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs did not personally decide state weighty affairs; all lawsuits were presided over only by the yilibi.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs did not personally decide major state matters; all lawsuits were handled by the yilibi alone.

sentences.zh: 及蕭合卓、蕭樸相繼為樞密使，專尚吏才，始自聽訟。

translations.literal: When Xiao Hezhuo and Xiao Pu succeeded one another as Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, valuing administrative talent exclusively, they began to hear lawsuits themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Hezhuo and Xiao Pu successively served as commissioners, prizing administrative talent, they began hearing lawsuits themselves.

sentences.zh: 時人轉相效習，以狡智相高，風俗自此衰矣。

translations.literal: People of the time imitated one another in turn, competing in cunning intelligence, and custom declined from this.
translations.idiomatic: Others followed suit, competing in cunning, and public morals declined from that point.

sentences.zh: 故太平六年下詔曰：「朕以國家有契丹、漢人，故以南、北二院分治之，蓋欲去貪枉，除煩擾也；

translations.literal: Therefore in the sixth year of Taiping an edict was issued: "We, considering that the state has Khitan and Han Chinese, therefore govern them separately through the Southern and Northern Courts, intending to remove corruption and injustice and eliminate vexatious trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the sixth year of Taiping an edict declared: "Our state has Khitan and Han subjects, whom we govern through separate Southern and Northern Courts, intending to remove corruption and eliminate vexation;

sentences.zh: 若貴賤異法，則怨必生。

translations.literal: if noble and humble are judged by different laws, resentment is sure to arise."
translations.idiomatic: if noble and humble are judged by different laws, resentment is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 夫小民犯罪，必不能動有司以達於朝，惟內族、外戚多恃恩行賄，以圖茍免，如是則法廢矣。

translations.literal: When common people commit offenses, they surely cannot move the authorities to reach the court; only inner-clan kin and outer-clan affines mostly rely on favor to offer bribes, seeking careless exemption — if so, the law is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who commit crimes cannot move the authorities to reach the throne; only imperial kin and affines rely on favor to bribe their way free — and thus the law falls into disuse.

sentences.zh: 自今貴戚以事被告，不以事之大小，並令所在官司按問，具申北、南院覆問得實以聞；

translations.literal: From now on, when nobles and affines are accused in any matter, regardless of its size, all local offices are ordered to investigate, report in full to the Northern and Southern Courts for re-examination, and memorialize the verified facts;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when nobles and affines are accused, regardless of the gravity of the offense, local offices must investigate and report to the Northern and Southern Courts for review before memorializing the throne;

sentences.zh: 其不按輒申，及受請托為奏言者，以本犯人罪罪之。

translations.literal: whoever investigates without due process and memorializes rashly, or accepts entreaties to speak on another's behalf, is to be punished with the same offense as the original criminal.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who investigates improperly, memorializes rashly, or accepts bribes to speak on a defendant's behalf shall be punished with the same offense as the accused.

sentences.zh: 」七年，詔中外大臣曰：「《制》條中有遺闕及輕重失中者，其條上之，議增改焉。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict to ministers inside and outside the court said: "Where provisions in the Regulations have omissions or where severity and leniency are imbalanced, memorialize the articles for discussion of additions and revisions."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict to all ministers declared: "Where provisions in the Regulations are missing or penalties are imbalanced, submit the articles for discussion of additions and revisions."
